::: {.lead}
Today you get a first draft from an AI assistant and put it into Word,
then you check and translate a report with the tools of Word. Each experiment has two parts. **Part
A** is in the AI assistant and Word on the lab computer. **Part B** is on a
simulator of the interactive lesson: on paper, scan its QR code; on the
screen, click its link. After each step, write your result in its box. At
the end, copy your key results into the table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with Word, a browser and an AI assistant
  that the university allows (for example `copilot.microsoft.com` with your
  university account).
- **No lab computer today?** Your teacher does Part A on the screen, on the
  simulators of the interactive lesson and in an AI assistant. Do Part B on your phone.
- **Never type personal data** into an AI tool: the start file has only
  made-up details.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

{{< start-files >}}

## Experiment 1 · A first draft from AI

**The idea:** AI writes a **first draft** or a **summary** fast: a notice,
an e-mail, the main points of a report. You give the facts in the prompt,
then you read every line: the AI can add facts that nobody gave, or change
a number, and you fix them. Paste into Word with **Keep Text Only**, so
that the styles of Word give the look.

**Aim:** a first draft from AI, with only your facts.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (an AI assistant and Word)**
:::

1. Copy the prompt into the AI assistant. Find every fact that you did
   **not** give.

   ::: {.prompt}
   Write a short notice for the staff of a small office. The printer on the
   first floor is broken. Please use the printer on the second floor until
   Tuesday. Three short lines.
   :::

   {{< record "Facts that I did not give (or: none)" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good draft has your three facts: the printer on the **first floor** is
   broken, use the printer on the **second floor**, until **Tuesday**. The
   AI often adds something, for example "A technician comes on Monday" or
   "Call IT on 123": nobody said it, so you delete it.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   A draft has five lines. Keep or delete? Sort them.

   Your fact: keep it
   :   The printer on the first floor is broken.

       Why: You gave this fact.

   :   Please use the printer on the second floor.

       Why: You gave this fact.

   :   You can use it until Tuesday.

       Why: Tuesday is in your prompt.

   Not given: delete it
   :   A technician comes on Monday.

       Why: Nobody said it: the AI invented it.

   :   Call IT on 123.

       Why: A phone number that nobody gave: delete it.
   :::

2. Paste the draft into Word with **Keep Text Only**, make the first line
   a **Title**, and save it as `printer-notice.docx`.

   {{< record "The file name" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   `printer-notice.docx`. **Keep Text Only** pastes only the words, without
   the look of the chat. Then the styles of Word give the look: the first
   line is a Title.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Why paste with **Keep Text Only**?

   - [x] It pastes only the words, without the look of the chat.

     Why: Then the styles of Word give the look.

   - [ ] It pastes the words and the colours of the chat.

     Why: That is Keep Source Formatting.

   - [ ] It deletes the facts that the AI added.

     Why: Only you can find and delete them.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/word-ai-lab.html" poster="sims/word-ai-lab.png" title="Word AI Lab: draft, sum up, rewrite, translate" >}}

3. In **Word AI Lab**, choose **Sum up** and tap the wrong part.

   {{< record "The wrong part, and the right fact" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   "Shop staff pick up the price list at **3 pm**": the memo says **5 pm**.
   A summary can change a number, so you find it in the original.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="5 pm|5|5pm|5 p.m.|17:00|5:00 pm" hint="Find the price list in the memo, not in the summary."}
   The summary says: "Shop staff pick up the price list at 3 pm." What time
   does the memo say?

   Why: The memo says 5 pm. A summary can change a number, so you check each one in the original.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · Check a report in Word

**The idea:** Word checks your text. A red wavy line marks a word that Word
does not know: a spelling mistake, or a name. **Review › Spelling** (**F7**)
shows each one: choose the right word, or **Ignore** for a name. **Find and
Replace** (**Ctrl + H**) changes a word or a number everywhere at once: a
date, a time, a name. **Review › Word Count** counts the words.

**Aim:** correct the spelling and change a time everywhere, with the tools
of Word.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. In `report-start.docx`, press **F7**. Correct the two mistakes, and
   **Ignore** names.

   {{< record "The two words, corrected" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **secnd → second** and **custmers → customers**. Word may also mark a
   name that it does not know (for example Zarqa or Saleh): choose
   **Ignore**, because a name is not a mistake.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Word marks **custmers** with a red line. Which suggestion do you choose?

   - [x] customers

     Why: The sentence is about the people who buy: customers.

   - [ ] costumers

     Why: A costume is clothing for a show: this word is wrong here.

   - [ ] Ignore

     Why: Ignore is for a name; custmers is a spelling mistake.
   :::

2. The shop now opens at 10:00. Press **Ctrl + H**, replace **9:00** with
   **10:00** (**Replace All**). How many replacements?

   {{< record "Replacements" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **2**: "next Saturday at 9:00" and "from 9:00 to 20:00". Replace All
   changes every one at once, so you miss none.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="2|two" hint="Look for 9:00 in the second and in the fourth paragraph."}
   The report has "next Saturday at 9:00" and "from 9:00 to 20:00". How many replacements does Replace All make?

   Why: 9:00 is in the report two times, so Word makes 2 replacements.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/check-lab.html" poster="sims/check-lab.png" title="Check Lab: spelling, Find and Replace" >}}

3. Do the two tasks of **Check Lab**: the spelling, then Find and Replace.

   {{< record "The number of replacements" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **2** replacements. The two red words are second and customers; Zarqa
   is a name, so you choose Ignore.
   :::

   ::: {.order}
   Put the steps of Find and Replace in order.

   1. Press Ctrl + H
   2. Type 9:00 in Find what
   3. Type 10:00 in Replace with
   4. Click Replace All

   Why: First open the box, then type what to find and the new text, then replace every one.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · A translation and the right tone

**The idea:** Word translates a short text in seconds: **Review ›
Translate**. A **machine translation** is fast, but check every day,
number and name in it. A **rewrite** says the same facts in other words,
and the **tone** fits the reader: formal for a customer that you do not
know, friendly for a friend. A rewrite or a translation changes the words,
never the facts.

**Aim:** the same facts in Arabic, and the right tone for each reader.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. In `report-start.docx`, select the second paragraph and choose **Review
   › Translate › Translate Selection** › **Arabic**. Check the day, the time
   and the names.

   {{< record "The day and the time in Arabic" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A right translation says **السبت** (Saturday) and **10:00** (the time
   after Experiment 2), and the names **الزرقاء** and **شارع الملك
   عبدالله**. No Translate in your Word? Use Word on the web.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which Arabic word is right for **Saturday**?

   - [x] السبت

     Why: السبت is Saturday.

   - [ ] الجمعة

     Why: الجمعة is Friday.

   - [ ] الأحد

     Why: الأحد is Sunday.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/tone-lab.html" poster="sims/tone-lab.png" title="Tone Lab: one message in three tones" >}}

2. Do the three tasks of **Tone Lab**.

   {{< record "Task 1 … ; Task 2 … ; Task 3 …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Task 1:** formal and short (a customer that you have never met).
   **Task 2:** friendly and short (a customer who is your friend).
   **Task 3:** formal and long (a letter for the company file).
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which tone and length fits each reader of Tone Lab? Sort them.

   Formal and short
   :   Mr Haddad, a big customer that you have never met

       Why: Formal for a person you do not know; short for an e-mail.

   Friendly and short
   :   Sami, a customer who is also your friend, in a chat

       Why: Friendly for a person you know well, in a chat.

   Formal and long
   :   a letter for the company file

       Why: A letter for the file needs all the facts, in a formal tone.
   :::
